notes.title: Update 1.3 – Non-integer scaling, gameplay + scoring changes, balancing
notes.content:
[u][b]Update 1.3 Patch Notes[/b][/u]

[b]Display[/b]
[list]
[*] The fullscreen option now uses Exclusive Fullscreen and non-integer scaling (this means the game will try to fit the entire screen in this setting and should also reduce input lag)
[/list]

[b]Gameplay[/b]
[list]
[*] You now create a small circular area at the end of each dash that clears projectiles for a fraction of a second. This should make dashing safer, as it gives you more time to readjust to the situation
[*] Dash now deals slightly more damage
[*] Enemies now blink when near death, indicating they can be killed with a single dash
[/list]

[b]Scoring[/b]
[list]
[*] You now start losing your chain multiplier after a 1.5s delay. Touching enemies with your shot, using your dash, and collecting HP pickups resets this duration. This allows you to maintain your multiplier across the entire level for a much higher score
[*] Your overall multiplier is now capped at ×16
[*] Reaching certain score thresholds rewards you with +1 HP (250000, 500000, 1000000, 2000000). Your score will become brighter and orange when you get close to these thresholds
[*] Style points are now awarded one by one during chains
[*] Bosses now display a timer in the top-right corner of your screen
[*] Using a non-damaging dash during a boss fight incurs a 20s penalty to the timer
[*] You are awarded points based on the time left when you defeat the boss
[*] Some transitions have been shortened slightly to prevent breaking your slice chain
[/list]

[b]Balancing[/b]
[u]Level 2[/u]
[list]
[*] Various enemies no longer deal contact damage
[*] Some attacks from the midboss have been toned down in both Novice and Arcade mode
[*] The boss now uses aimed projectiles in Phases 1 and 3 instead of random bursts of projectiles
[/list]

[u]Level 3[/u]
[list]
[*] The Eel's fire rate has been reduced
[*] The Jellyfish wave now behaves differently to be slightly more dangerous
[*] The Brain bonus boss no longer deals contact damage
[/list]

[b]Visibility[/b]
[list]
[*] Jellyfish in the background of Level 3 have been resprited to be less distracting
[*] Shockwave attacks in Level 3 are now slightly brighter.
[*] Missile projectiles have been resprited to be brighter.
[*] The first boss's laser is now displayed on a lower layer so it does not hide projectiles during the fight.
[*] The tentacles of Jellyfish enemies are now brighter.
[/list]

[b]Music[/b]
[list]
[*] The track Hope of Molybdion was changed for better mixing.
[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed a crash that occurred when using the mouse to spam-click certain buttons.
[/list]

notes.title: Lilac 0: Scoring guide
notes.content:
[h3][b]With the Lilac 0 demo now live and the full release fast approaching (4th March!), we wanted to give some extra insight into the game's scoring system. On a basic level, it's about consecutively killing as many enemies as you can without taking a hit, but the guide below will help you keep the multiplier high and maximise scoring potential. [/b][/h3]

[u][h3][b]LILAC 0: SCORING SYSTEM GUIDE[/b][/h3] [/u]

[list]
[*] When killing an enemy, the score multiplier in the top right slightly increases (+0.1). This continues until it reaches a limit of (x8.0). Missing an enemy (meaning it leaves the screen before dying) lowers it by (-0.5), and getting hit makes it drop by (-4.0) .

[*] The score multiplier does not carry over to boss fights.
 
[*] When slicing enemies, it begins a 'slice chain'. The score multiplier turns from purple to orange and each enemy killed during the chain increases the multiplier by (0.5). This allows the multiplier to rise above the (x8.0) threshold.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308837/41b750a02e41a0ede6c90b7e8dcb0142f642fc65.gif[/img]
 
[*] If you don't slice another enemy within 1 second, the slice chain is broken, and the score multiplier reverts to purple.
 
[*] Every 3 enemies killed during a slice chain awards you style points. 

[*] Scanning enemies to damage them is effectively the same as slicing them with a dash. You can mix scan and slice kills to keep a slice chain going.
 
[*] Style points are also awarded for overkilling sub-bosses and bosses. Every end of level boss can be overkilled when certain conditions are met. For example, to overkill the Level 1 boss, you must dash through it while it traverses the screen during its last attack.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308837/fc52b7be87d5a1d156f0c6393648fbd606f864c4.gif[/img]

[*] Overkilling bosses also awards more points than simply beating them normally.

[*] A 'Style' rating is given at the end of every level. More style points = a higher rating, with 'S' being the highest. Ratings are also given at the end of the level for 'Miss' and 'Kill'. Miss = how successfully you evaded enemies and bullets (i.e. not being hit). Kill = how many enemies you killed. 

[*] Based on the end of level ratings, additional points are awarded to the score tally. An S rating is worth +10000 points, so it's possible to gain a maximum of +30000 points at the end of each level. 
 
[*] There are also other minor ways of getting more points, such as grabbing an HP pickup when your health is already full. 

[/list]

We hope you're enjoying the demo. You'll be able to experience the full game when it launches 4th March. Thanks for playing!

notes.title: Lilac 0 – a vertical shmup with a classic arcade feel
notes.content:
We're proud to present Lilac 0 – a vertically scrolling shoot 'em up set on the machine world of Molybdion. You control Rairakku, an ancient warrior and blade-wielding automaton deployed to destroy the planet's mechanzied inhabitants. 

Lilac 0 is created by Victor Pouderoux. A regular on the French game jam scene, this is the first project he's developed to completion. The game has a retro arcade feel that combines refined mechanics, challenging gameplay, stunning pixel art and a powerful chiprock soundtrack. There are 5 levels (starting in the clouds high above Molybdion and descending deep below the planet's surface), 3 difficulty levels, 8 different color palettes, and 2 playable characters.

The game features a lock-on system that slows down your movement for greater precision and allows you to target your opponents before cutting them into pieces. More unusually, the game also features a dash move. In addition to making the player momentarily invulnerable, the dash is the only way to defeat certain enemies. It’s also used to execute an "overkill" a special finisher move that slices its target in two and awards lots of score. 

Check out the announcement trailer:

[previewyoutube=7y9xFS1BPP0;full][/previewyoutube]

We're aiming to launch Lilac 0 early 2025, but will be releasing a demo before then. Be sure to Wishlist and Follow to be notified when the demo is available, and when the full game releases. 

ONE AGAINST ALL!
